fixes.explanation: Martha and Mary are real people in Luke, friend. They're sisters, and Luke 10:38 says Martha welcomed Jesus into her home. But they aren't the visitors here. Luke 8:19 says it's Jesus' mother and brothers who came. Easy mix-up, since Luke has so many people showing up at once.
Right, friend. Luke 8:19 says they were unable to reach Him because of the crowd. No walking up to Him. Then Luke 8:20 says He was told they were there, and that's what happens next.

You got it, baker. Someone tells Jesus, "Your mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to see You." (Luke 8:20) They're standing right there, just on the wrong side of that crowd. I think that has to feel rough, standing out there while a whole crowd stays put.

Upstairs is a fun guess, friend, but that's not the word. Luke 8:20 says they are standing outside, wanting to see Him. The text gives us that one word, so I'll stick with outside. Nothing in the story points upstairs.

Close, baker, but it's the opposite word. Luke 8:20 says His mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to see Him. Luke 8:19 says the crowd kept them from reaching Him. So outside is the word that fits.

Sitting close sounds right, baker. But Jesus doesn't talk about who sits where. He says, "My mother and brothers are those who hear the word of God and carry it out." (Luke 8:21) Listening is only half of it. The doing is the other half.
